title: Stationarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Time Series Forecasting

problem.claim: Real-world time series exhibit non-stationarity and regime shifts that challenge fully parametric forecasters.

gap.claim: Similarity-only retrieval is brittle and redundant because a similar past segment may not imply a similar future under non-stationarity.

contributions.claim: SARAF adaptively balances relevance and diversity in retrieval for time series forecasting.
SARAF constructs candidates using temporal similarity with time-aligned enhancement and selects diverse historical regimes with diversification strength modulated by dataset-level stationarity.
SARAF uses stationarity-aware aggregation to fuse retrieved futures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight real-world datasets report competitive forecasting performance and improved average accuracy and robustness over strong baselines.
The authors report particularly clear benefits under challenging non-stationary settings.
Code is provided at the reported GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series forecasting depends on historical patterns but is challenged by non-stationarity and regime shifts.
Retrieval-augmented forecasters use relevant historical segments as external inference-time evidence.
Similarity-only retrieval can fail and become redundant when historical series are non-stationary.
SARAF combines stationarity-aware retrieval, diversity modulation, and stationarity-aware future aggregation.
Experiments on eight real-world datasets report competitive performance, improved accuracy and robustness, and stronger benefits in non-stationary settings.

source_observation.claim: Under non-stationarity, historical similarity alone may not identify futures that remain useful for forecasting.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval systems for changing temporal environments may need to balance relevance with coverage of heterogeneous regimes.

application.claim: When applying retrieval to non-stationary sequential data, evaluate diversity-aware selection and condition retrieval strength on stationarity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that stationarity-aware retrieval is preferable for stationary datasets or all forecasting settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the eight datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the stationarity measure or how diversification strength is computed.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols, ablations, or statistical uncertainty.
